capabilities.complete_execution: At most one model-selected changed candidate, complete simulation, unchanged reach evaluation and sampled holding/profile feedback.
capabilities.local_comparison: Optional one paired local comparison, two solves, <=300 charged seconds, at a saved baseline update with effective horizon 0.01 s; select one changed positive weight. Existing previous-input cold seed and integration retained. Unavailable/inconclusive screening does not prohibit a justified complete experiment.

control/recipe/holding_tip_speed_weight.description: Per-second squared spatial speed weight on nodes at/after the configured task settling-window start. Requires explicit settling settings.

control/recipe/terminal_tip_speed_weight.description: Dimensionless terminal weight on squared world tip speed / tip_speed_scale_m_s. Zero preserves legacy cost.

instructions: Read the accepted diagnosis and supplied two-path control grant. Independently select whether to change one or both weights and their values: adopt with a nonempty effective delta, or defer/reject with empty changes for a specific evidence, feasibility, scope or budget reason. Missing proof of causality alone does not prohibit this bounded experiment. State a concrete hypothesis, why the weight is relevant, expected effects separately on reach, holding position, holding speed and computation, possible adverse effects, and observations that would weaken the hypothesis. Both bounds are [0,1]; newly positive values must be >=0.0001. All other scientific fields are fixed. Preserve terminal speed cost as a single terminal scaled squared-speed term, and holding speed cost as an integration-step-weighted sum at scheduled holding nodes; scale and scheduling remain unchanged. Do not compare raw scalar objectives across weights. Optionally request local_comparison for one selected positive changed parameter and a legal saved update (effective horizon 0.01 s). The pair is advisory, at most two solves and 300 charged seconds. Unavailable/inconclusive local screening permits the complete experiment. Do not select a developer-prescribed value or force adoption. Availability status applies to the entire inventory entry unless you supply update_ids (controller updates) or time_range_s (sampled backend motion). For a partially read entry, use queried and describe missing coverage, or explicitly scope a not_read/not_displayed declaration to the unread subset.

recommendations.rationale: Retained signals describe the unsettled window (sampled speed above the 0.02 m/s limit at every instant, error above the 0.01 m limit at some instants) and show horizon/solver variation, but none isolates a dominant cause and no closed-loop counterfactual replay is available. Defer any control-parameter change until a bounded comparison is run.

If a bounded complete experiment is later authorized, the explicit control grant permits changing only terminal_tip_speed_weight or holding_tip_speed_weight; this phase selects neither parameter nor value, and any such trial should keep reach evaluation unchanged and read out the sampled holding window.

attribution.reason: Every sampled holding-window speed (0.6352-1.5810 m/s) lies far above the 0.02 m/s settling limit and peak sampled error reaches 0.0581381 m, so the window is observed unsettled with the tip still moving. This is an observation of window state, not a proven cause of the miss.

Only 6 noninitialization updates were selected of 35, stopping is dominated by User_Requested_Stop (34) with a single Solve_Succeeded, and mean update wall is ~17.26 s against a 0.01 s period. Synchronous wall overruns do not by themselves establish skipped simulated backend updates, so an association between the small number of applied control updates and the unsettled window remains possible but unproven.

Effective horizon (10 down to 1 control intervals), solver raw status (User_Requested_Stop vs Solve_Succeeded) and projection residual (~2.1-2.7 rad/m) do vary by update, but no full warm plans or optimizer iteration traces are retained, so these records cannot be linked to the holding-window outcome.

facts.statement: Baseline run cf997605885642759ee33920e2c9e2ef records reach_passed=true with terminal_error_m 0.0076426 m below the 0.01 m reach tolerance, while holding_position_passed=false and joint_reach_holding_passed=false against settling limits of 0.01 m and 0.02 m/s.

Across all 6 recorded final-holding-window samples (0.30-0.35 s) sampled error spans 0.0076426-0.0581381 m and sampled speed spans 0.6352-1.5810 m/s; the minimum window speed equals the recorded terminal_speed_m_s 0.6352 m/s and late_max_error_m is 0.0581381 m, so no sampled instant is inside the 0.02 m/s or 0.01 m limits.

Computation: mean_update_s 17.2633 s against control_period_s 0.01 s, deadline_misses 35 with update_count 35, noninitialization_selected 6, and stopping counts of User_Requested_Stop 34 versus Solve_Succeeded 1.

Retained plan/solver records vary across updates: effective_horizon takes 10, 5, 2 and 1 control intervals at updates 23, 30, 33, 34; optimization_raw_status is User_Requested_Stop at update 30 and Solve_Succeeded at update 34; projection_residual_rad_m is about 2.10-2.74 rad/m; recorded recipe values include holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0 and terminal_velocity_weight 0.0001 (configuration only, no cost-contribution data retained).

limitations: No closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal attribution capability; a single execution and model comparisons do not establish a dominant cause.
Motion display covers only the final 0.30-0.35 s window; prediction/plans views cover only selected updates, so cited ranges are selected-row coverage, not whole-trajectory statements.
Projected GVS one-step comparisons are bounded-horizon probes and cannot explain the entire settling failure; full state agreement is not retained.
Raw weight magnitudes do not establish cost-term importance without actual cost contributions and scaling, which are not retained.

request_content.question: Baseline run cf997605885642759ee33920e2c9e2ef (35 updates over 0.00-0.35 s) reaches but does not hold. Reach passes: reach_passed true, terminal_error_m 0.00764 m below the 0.01 m reach tolerance [fb51f58c86383, f32499be1bfe7, fb1126088442c]. Holding fails: holding_position_passed, holding_speed_passed and joint_reach_holding_passed are all false [fe14a467a41f7, f85d7117f58c4, fcca534323073]. In the final 0.05 s holding window (samples 0.30-0.35 s) sampled error spans 0.00764-0.05814 m and sampled speed spans 0.635-1.581 m/s, both far outside the 0.01 m and 0.02 m/s settling limits [f5bc8769c993b, fcdb037491931, fdad3b4c317ee, fd52e841c473a, f1db2acbe8c84, f04eefc525d88, fd72daef26b22]. Computation is grossly over budget: mean_update_s 17.26 s against a 0.01 s control period, 35/35 deadline misses, and only 6 noninitialization updates selected against 35 total [f50ad1901565c, ff5d8adf94047, fef0780bf697f, f3e6e47bc4c35, f0503bfb7418a, f20c1f5e0b3fa]. Open question: across the retained one_step_predictions, saved_projected_states, plan_selection, solver_status, controller_horizon and derived backend_motion records, what retained signals discriminate whether the unsettled holding window is associated with (a) the small number of controller updates actually applied under the overrun, (b) a terminal state that enters the window already moving (terminal_speed_m_s 0.635 m/s, late_max_speed 1.581 m/s) [fbb622a68c8d2, fa3ce632d6e5d], or (c) plan-selection/solver behavior varying across updates (optimization_selected_iteration, optimization_raw_status)? Can these retained signals be evaluated without a closed-loop counterfactual replay, and where do they leave the question under-constrained? No dominant cause and no winning parameter is presumed.
scope: Retained-evidence reading and reporting only, via diagnosis.inspect_evidence views (motion, prediction, plans) over chosen update_ids (at most 8 per query) and/or evidence.read on JSON-addressable records: one_step_prediction, measured_initial_state, actual_tension_n, optimization_selected_iteration, optimization_raw_status, effective_horizon.
